# T4.4 (TASKS.md) -- heir selection + announcement. With HeirElection on, the
# leader ranks eligible followers by stability score once per heartbeat
# interval (DESIGN.md §2.3) and announces the winner by piggybacking a Heir
# field on MsgHeartbeat/MsgApp (§2.4); `status` surfaces the leader's own
# heir + churn count (added to BasicStatus for this task -- see
# rafttest/interaction_env_handler_status.go). Written first per the TDD
# convention in CLAUDE.md, before selectHeir/heirEligible/changeHeir landed
# in raft.go.

log-level error
----
ok

# Cluster A: three voters added one at a time (same voters= set each call)
# so each can carry its own constant stability score -- id 3 is highest and
# should end up heir once the leader's first heartbeat tick runs selection.
add-nodes 1 voters=(1,2,3) index=2 heir-election=true stability-score=50
----
ok

add-nodes 1 voters=(1,2,3) index=2 heir-election=true stability-score=100
----
ok

add-nodes 1 voters=(1,2,3) index=2 heir-election=true stability-score=255
----
ok

----
ok

status 1
----
1: StateReplicate match=3 next=4
2: StateReplicate match=3 next=4 score=100
3: StateReplicate match=3 next=4 score=255
heir=3 churn=0

# Node 2 campaigns with a higher term while 1 is still leader. Per vanilla
# Raft term rules, 1 steps down to follower on the higher term before this
# resolves -- (*raft).reset clears its heir soft state (DESIGN.md §2.4: soft
# state, lost on term change). This is the T4.4 accept criterion ("heir
# cleared on term change"): 1 is no longer leader (so its Progress map is
# empty) and its heir is back to None/churn 0, so the status command below
# has nothing to print at all -- the plain "ok" is the proof, matching
# Cluster B's off-by-default output exactly. Compare against the
# heir=3 churn=0 line above, which is what an unreset heir would still show.
campaign 2
----
ok
